## Answers

**h01** — `s3presign.Runner` (`server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:16`) — re-presigns S3 object URLs so stored `reference` links don't expire — every **12 hours** (`runnerInterval = time.Hour * 12`, `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:27`; loop at `:29-41`), refreshing any object whose presign is <4 days from its 5-day expiry (`:85-91`) — wired in `Server.startBackgroundRunners`: constructed `server/server.go:162`, run once immediately at `server/server.go:163`, goroutine started at `server/server.go:169`; `startBackgroundRunners` is called from `Server.Start` at `server/server.go:129`.

**h02** — Delivery function: `webhook.Post` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:120` (the actual `safeClient.Do(req)` is at `:152`); async entry `webhook.PostAsync` `:184` feeds a 128-slot queue drained by 4 goroutines (`:39-55`).
Protection: two layers — (a) dial-time SSRF guard `safeDialContext` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:59-77`) installed as the shared client's `Transport.DialContext` (`:32-37`), which resolves the host and rejects reserved/private IPs (also defeats DNS rebinding); (b) `webhook.ValidateURL` at registration time (`internal/webhook/validate.go:62`), enforcing http/https and non-reserved resolution, called from `server/router/api/v1/user_service_webhooks.go:74,161,182`. Reserved CIDRs at `internal/webhook/validate.go:14-23`; escape hatch `AllowPrivateIPs` (`validate.go:41`) set from the `--allow-private-webhooks` flag at `cmd/memos/main.go:49` (default false, `:133`).

**h03** — Abstraction package: `internal/idp` (`internal/idp/idp.go:1`, defines `IdentityProviderUserInfo`); concrete implementation package: `internal/idp/oauth2` (`internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go:1`, `IdentityProvider` at `:19`, `NewIdentityProvider` at `:27`). OAuth2 is the only protocol implementation shipped.

**h04** — **No.** The only construction site is `mysql.NewDB(profile)` in the factory `NewDBDriver` at `store/db/db.go:22`. A repo-wide grep for `mysql.NewDB` / `&mysql.` / `mysql.Driver{` over all `*.go` returns exactly that one hit; the other `mysql` references in `store/test/containers.go` are the testcontainers module and the `go-sql-driver/mysql` DSN parser, not the memos driver type.

**h05** — Mechanism: **explicit Go code**, per-driver, inside the delete-user transaction — not a DB rule.
- `store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go:96` (`deleteReactionsByContentIDsTx`, defined `:380`) and `:102` (`deleteReactionsByCreatorTx`, defined `:400`)
- Same pair in `store/db/postgres/user_delete.go:96,102,380,400` and `store/db/mysql/user_delete.go:96,102,417,437`
- Evidence there is no DB-level rule: the `reaction` table declares no foreign key in any dialect (`store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql:92-99`, `store/migration/postgres/LATEST.sql:91-98`, `store/migration/mysql/LATEST.sql:91-98`); the only `ON DELETE CASCADE` in the schemas is on `memo_share.memo_id` (`store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql:109` and peers), and SQLite runs with FKs disabled anyway (`_pragma=foreign_keys(0)`, `store/db/sqlite/sqlite.go:53`).

**h06** — Handlers (all `APIV1Service`):
- `CreateMemo` — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:70` → `DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook` at `:157`
- `UpdateMemo` — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:401` → `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects` at `:513` → `DispatchMemoUpdatedWebhook` (`memo_update_helpers.go:67`)
- `DeleteMemo` — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:518` → `DispatchMemoDeletedWebhook` at `:562`
- `CreateMemoComment` — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go:20` → `DispatchMemoCommentCreatedWebhook` at `:119`
- Also `SetMemoRelations` (`memo_relation_service.go:16`→`:48`) and `SetMemoAttachments` (`memo_attachment_service.go:16`→`:48`)

Convergence function: **`webhook.Post`** — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:120` (all paths funnel through `webhook.PostAsync`, `memo_service_webhooks.go:43,71` → queue → `Post`).

**h07**
- Route `GET /file/users/:identifier/avatar` — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:124` (registered from `server/server.go:82`)
- `FileServerService.serveUserAvatar` — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:168`
- `FileServerService.getUserByUsername` — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:715`
- `store.Store.GetUser` — `store/user.go:148` (username lookup bypasses `userCache`, which is keyed by ID at `store/user.go:150`)
- `store.Store.ListUsers` — `store/user.go:136` → `s.driver.ListUsers` (interface `store/driver.go:47`)
- `sqlite.DB.ListUsers` — `store/db/sqlite/user.go:88` (default driver) — reads `user.avatar_url`
- Back in the handler: `parseDataURI` decodes the stored base64 data URI — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:196`, MIME allow-list `:74-75`, blob written `:208`

**h08**
- `*memopayload.Runner.RunOnce` — `server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:27` — **not invoked** anywhere (no caller in production or test code)
- `*s3presign.Runner.RunOnce` — `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:43` — **invoked** — callers: `server/server.go:163` (`startBackgroundRunners`) and `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:36` (its own ticker loop)

**h09** — **6** declarations in backend Go (8 if the two `_test.go` helpers at `store/test/filter_helpers_test.go:200,282` are counted). Invoked by non-test server code:
- `*store.Store.Close` (`store/store.go:72`) — caller `server/server.go:146` (`Server.Shutdown`)
- `*SSEHub.Close` (`server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go:99`) — caller `server/server.go:206` (`closeLongLivedConnections`)
- `*cache.Cache.Close` (`store/cache/cache.go:187`) — callers `store/store.go:74,75,76`
- `*sqlite.DB.Close` (`store/db/sqlite/sqlite.go:67`) — via `s.driver.Close()` at `store/store.go:78` (this is the one that runs by default); `*postgres.DB.Close` (`store/db/postgres/postgres.go:46`) and `*mysql.DB.Close` (`store/db/mysql/mysql.go:47`) are reachable through the same interface call only when those drivers are selected.

**h10** — `(*filter.Engine).CompileToStatement` — `internal/filter/engine.go:74` — **≈36 distinct callers** (next: `filter.NewEngine`, `internal/filter/engine.go:24`, ≈32). Most callers are `internal/filter`'s own tests; the 6 non-test callers are `internal/filter/helpers.go#AppendConditions`, `server/router/api/v1/attachment_service.go:413`, `server/router/api/v1/shortcut_service.go:356`, and `ListMemoRelations` in each of `store/db/{sqlite,postgres,mysql}/memo_relation.go`. Note: the index's two highest raw counts — `SortVersion.Len` (`internal/version/version.go:44`, 180) and `cronSchedule.Next` (`internal/scheduler/parser.go:92`, 57) — are name-collision artifacts (builtin `len(...)` and `sql.Rows.Next()`), not real fan-in. Restricted to non-test callers only, the top is `addArg` (`internal/filter/render.go:842`, 14 callers, all within `render.go`).

**h11** — 1st: **`store.User`** (`store/user.go:29`) — referenced from ~6 non-test packages (`server/auth`, `server/notification`, `server/router/api/v1`, `server/router/fileserver`, `server/router/rss`, plus `server/router/api/v1/test`), ~71 references. 2nd: **`store.Memo`** (`store/memo.go:35`) — ~4 non-test packages (`server/notification`, `server/router/api/v1`, `server/router/rss`, `server/runner/memopayload`), ~51 references. (Next: `store.Attachment`, ~3 packages.)

**h12** — Concrete method: **`(*sqlite.DB).CreateMemo`** — `store/db/sqlite/memo.go:16` (the `INSERT INTO \`memo\` ... RETURNING` at `:41-42`).
Determination: the default of the `--driver` flag is `sqlite` (`cmd/memos/main.go:122` `viper.SetDefault("driver","sqlite")` and `:130`), which flows into `Profile.Driver` (`cmd/memos/main.go:43`) and then into the factory switch `db.NewDBDriver` (`store/db/db.go:19-20`), selecting `sqlite.NewDB`. That value is stored as `Store.driver` (`store/store.go`, via `store.New` at `cmd/memos/main.go:64`), and the call chain is `APIV1Service.CreateMemo` (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:70`) → `Store.CreateMemo` (`store/memo.go:109`) → `s.driver.CreateMemo` (`store/memo.go:113`, interface `store/driver.go`) → the sqlite implementation. The mysql/postgres implementations of the same interface method are the other candidates and only run with `--driver mysql|postgres`.

**h13** — Impl: the unexported `markdown.service` struct (`internal/markdown/markdown.go:58`), the sole implementation of `markdown.Service` (`internal/markdown/markdown.go:31`).
Construction: `markdown.NewService(...)` (`internal/markdown/markdown.go:85`), called in production at `server/router/api/v1/v1.go:48` with `WithTagExtension()` + `WithMentionExtension()` (also `server/router/api/v1/test/test_helper.go:44` for tests).
Holders of the interface: `APIV1Service.MarkdownService` (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:36`, assigned `:56`), `rss.RSSService.MarkdownService` (`server/router/rss/rss.go:62`, wired from `server/server.go:85`), and `memopayload.Runner.MarkdownService` (`server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:16`).

**h14** — Computation site: `memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload` — `server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:74`, which delegates to `markdownService.ExtractAll` (`internal/markdown/markdown.go:356`) and assigns `memo.Payload.Tags` and `memo.Payload.Property` (`runner.go:85-86`).
Triggers: `APIV1Service.CreateMemo` — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:108`; `APIV1Service.UpdateMemo` (on content change) — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:447`; and the bulk backfill `memopayload.Runner.RunOnce` — `server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:52` (declared but never invoked, see h08).
Extracted: `Tags` (deduped `#tag` list), and `Property` — `Title` (leading H1 text), `HasLink`, `HasCode` (code block/span), `HasTaskList`, `HasIncompleteTasks` (`internal/markdown/markdown.go:378-410`); `Mentions` are also produced by `ExtractAll` but not stored in the payload.

**h15** — Distinct enforcement sites:
- `APIV1Service.checkMemoReadAccess` (single-memo gRPC reads) — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:39-68` (visibility branch `:55-66`)
- `APIV1Service.ListMemos` visibility narrowing — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:219-226`
- `APIV1Service.ListAllUserStats` / `GetUserStats` — `server/router/api/v1/user_service_stats.go:84,90,218,220`
- `FileServerService.checkAttachmentPermission` (HTTP file server) — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:677,699`
- `SSEClient.canReceive` (event stream fan-out) — `server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go:134-142`
- Reaction service — `server/router/api/v1/reaction_service.go:30-38` and `:83`
- Attachment services — `server/router/api/v1/attachment_service.go:445-451` and `server/router/api/v1/memo_attachment_service.go:214-222`
- Comment creation/listing — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go:41`, `:100`
- RSS feeds (PUBLIC only) — `server/router/rss/rss.go:90,141`
- Frontend SSR metadata (PUBLIC only) — `server/router/frontend/frontend.go:150`
- Mention notifications — `server/router/api/v1/memo_mention_helpers.go:62,67,84`; email notification gating — `server/notification/email.go:313-316`, `server/router/api/v1/user_service_notifications.go:309-312`

**r01** — Premise is wrong: there is **no Redis** anywhere in the repo (no `redis` import in `go.mod` or any `.go` file). Caching is an in-process, in-memory implementation: `store/cache/cache.go` (`Interface` at `:10`, `Cache.Close` at `:187`). The store creates three of them — `instanceSettingCache`, `userCache`, `userSettingCache` — in `store.New` at `store/store.go:51-53`, all sharing one config built at `store/store.go:39-44`: `DefaultTTL: 10 * time.Minute`, `CleanupInterval: 5 * time.Minute`, `MaxItems: 1000`. So user entries expire after **10 minutes**, and the cache is keyed by user ID only (`store/user.go:88,150`) — username lookups miss it entirely.

**r02** — Premise is wrong: there is **no per-user API rate-limiting middleware** in this codebase. The only middleware registered on the Echo server is `middleware.Recover()` and CORS (`server/server.go:51-52`), plus the gRPC-Gateway auth middleware / Connect auth interceptor in `server/router/api/v1/v1.go:69-95`. The nearest throttling constructs are concurrency semaphores, not rate limits: `thumbnailSemaphore` (3) and `imageProcessingSemaphore` (2) at `server/router/api/v1/v1.go:59-60`, a request-size cap `maxAPIRequestBytes` (`v1.go:20`), and the 128-entry bounded webhook dispatch queue (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:39`). The only textual "rate limit" hit in the repo is a doc comment suggesting it as future work (`internal/email/doc.go:86`).

**r03** — Premise is wrong: there is **no nightly database-cleanup job and no cron scheduler running in the server**. A cron-capable package exists (`internal/scheduler`, cron parsing at `internal/scheduler/parser.go`, `Scheduler.Register` at `internal/scheduler/scheduler.go:70`), but it is imported only by its own tests (`internal/scheduler/example_test.go:10`, `internal/scheduler/integration_test.go:13`) — nothing under `server/` or `cmd/` registers a job. The only background work started at runtime is the S3 presign runner on a 12-hour ticker (`server/server.go:153-174`, `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:27`).

**r04** — Premise is wrong: there is **no message broker at all** — no NATS, RabbitMQ/AMQP, or Kafka in `go.mod` or any Go file, and no queue is declared anywhere. Webhook delivery uses an in-process Go channel: `asyncPostQueue = make(chan *WebhookRequestPayload, 128)` at `internal/webhook/webhook.go:39`, drained by 4 goroutines started in `init()` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:42-55`), each calling `webhook.Post` (`:120`). Producers call `webhook.PostAsync` (`:184`), which drops the payload with a warning when the buffer is full — so pending deliveries do not survive a restart.

**r05** — Premise is wrong: there is **no GraphQL schema** — no `graphql` dependency, schema file, or resolver in the repo. The public API is **gRPC defined in Protocol Buffers** under `proto/api/v1` (generated to `proto/gen/api/v1`), exposed over HTTP two ways from `APIV1Service.RegisterGateway` (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:65`): a grpc-gateway REST/JSON mux (handlers registered at `server/router/api/v1/v1.go:96-120` for Instance, Auth, User, Memo, Attachment, AI, Shortcut, IdentityProvider services) and Connect handlers. Alongside it are plain HTTP surfaces: the file server (`server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:121`), RSS (`server/router/rss/rss.go`), SSE, and MCP (`server/server.go:92-96`).
